name: rescript
tagline: Transcript-based video and audio editor that lives in the browser
description: rescript is an open-source, transcript-based media editor: drop in a video or audio file and it is transcribed locally with per-word timestamps and speaker labels, then you edit the media by editing the text. Delete words in the transcript and the corresponding clip is cut; remove fillers like um and uh or silences of 0.3s or more in one click; and export the final cut as video (MP4/WebM, 720p–4K), audio, transcript, or subtitles — without your file ever leaving your device. Transcription runs with Whisper via transformers.js in a Web Worker with WebGPU and WASM fallback, speaker labels come from pyannote, and export is frame-accurate via ffmpeg.wasm. It works fully in the browser at app.getrescript.com or as a signed Electron desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux, and also accepts imported SRT/VTT/JSON transcripts.
highlights: Edit video and audio by editing the transcript — delete words and the cut follows
Fully on-device: Whisper transcription, pyannote diarization, ffmpeg.wasm export, no uploads
One-click filler and silence removal, plus split, trim, and word-level timing fixes
Exports MP4/WebM (720p–4K), M4A/MP3/WAV, and SRT/VTT/JSON subtitles
Browser app plus signed Electron desktop builds for macOS, Windows, and Linux
curatorNote: Transcript-first editing done right — private by design, genuinely useful one-click cuts, and a polished web app with 714 stars in under two weeks. The polyform license keeps it noncommercial, but the tech is open and impressive.
